$comment: Nautilus PRD document format, doc_schema_version 2: Tiptap/ProseMirror JSON stored in prd.content_json.
Shared by the backend validator (app/backend/prd_document.py) and, later, the frontend's Tiptap setup.
Human-readable notes, examples and open questions: docs/prd-document-format.md.

status: agreed = settled in Backend Tasks v1.2 S03, M2 1.5, the frontend guide section 8, or confirmed with frontend (2026-10-29; editor compatibility confirmed by Aksh in a Discord DM to Marco, 2026-10-30);
agreed table and link settings below were finalized by Marco (2026-10-30) for the editor configuration;
proposed = written down here so it can be reviewed, NOT settled; reserved = defined but rejected until enabled.
DRAFT: nothing reads this file in production yet, and saves do not use it.

max_document_bytes.note: UTF-8 size of the compact JSON encoding. The database also caps pg_column_size(content_json) at 1 MB.

max_title_chars.note: PRD title, which is a column, not part of the document.

max_description_chars.note: PRD description column (S03/E05). Not part of the document.

max_depth.note: Nesting depth of nodes, counting doc as 1. Guards the validator against pathological input.

max_errors.note: The validator stops collecting after this many errors.

section_types.note: The nine allowed section types, in standard order. Titles are the display names used by the current frontend and seed data.

doc.note: A saved draft may have zero sections: {"type": "doc", "content": []}.

section.note: The visible section label is derived from attrs.type (agreed) and is not repeated inside content.

tableCell.note: Simple tables, no merged cells (Marco's implementation choice, 2026-10-30): colspan and rowspan are absent, null or 1 (Tiptap writes 1); the editor turns off mergeCells/splitCell. colwidth keeps column resizing: null or one whole-number width in pixels.

tableHeader.note: Simple tables, no merged cells (Marco's implementation choice, 2026-10-30): colspan and rowspan are absent, null or 1 (Tiptap writes 1); the editor turns off mergeCells/splitCell. colwidth keeps column resizing: null or one whole-number width in pixels.

text.note: Non-empty string. The only node that may carry marks.

link.note: Final settings (Marco, 2026-10-30): absolute http, https or mailto links of at most 2048 characters. target, rel and class are accepted only with the values Tiptap's Link extension writes by default; nothing else.

ai_generated.note: Provenance hint. Applied by the backend to accepted AI text, never by the model. Not inclusive at its edges; typing inside it may inherit it (agreed with frontend). This package checks only the attribute's shape; checking that the id names a successful generation_record for the same PRD needs the database and comes with S03 integration.

citation.note: Reserved until sources are developed (A09 stores sources at PRD level only). Rejected.

assumption.note: Marks text a person should check. Users can add it, and so can the one-time v1 conversion (DB07, from <mark class="nt-assumption">). AI output can never add it (see generation.forbid_marks). It is not provenance and never merges with ai_generated. Agreed with Aksh (Discord DM, 2026-10-30).

unique_section_types.note: Each section type appears at most once.

standard_section_order.note: Sections that are present appear in standard order. Saved drafts may hold any ordered subset, including none.

no_input_repair.note: Invalid input is rejected with errors, never fixed silently.

generation.note: Extra checks for complete initial-generation output (A01/A03), on top of every document rule above. Implemented in app/backend/ai/generation_output.py. Review readiness is a separate, later check: structural validity alone does not make a PRD ready for review.

require_all_sections.note: All nine sections, in standard order.

forbid_marks.note: Model output cannot set provenance (the backend adds ai_generated after validation) and cannot add assumption highlights (only people and the v1 conversion add them).

forbid_leading_section_title_heading.note: Section labels are derived from attrs.type, so generated content must not start with a heading that repeats the label. Saved drafts are not checked for this, since users may type any heading.
